claims.claim: Kaggle competitions use a holdout set for public rankings and a separate test set used once for final rankings, and a meta-analysis of over one hundred competitions found little evidence of substantial overfitting to the holdout set.
claims.quote: In each competition, numerous practitioners repeatedly evaluated their progress against a holdout set that forms the basis of a public ranking available throughout the competition. Performance on a separate test set used only once determined the final ranking.

claims.claim: The authors call for the community to actively develop fresh one-time exams to evaluate models accurately because string matching decontamination is insufficient and paraphrased test data can bypass it.
claims.quote: We urge the community to adopt stronger decontamination approaches when using public benchmarks. Moreover, we call for the community to actively develop fresh one-time exams to evaluate models accurately.

claims.claim: A differential-privacy-based algorithm enables reuse of a holdout set to validate many adaptively chosen hypotheses while provably avoiding overfitting to the holdout set itself.
claims.quote: We give a simple and practical method for reusing a holdout (or testing) set to validate the accuracy of hypotheses produced by a learning algorithm operating on a training set. Reusing a holdout set adaptively multiple times can easily lead to overfitting to the holdout set itself. We give an algorithm that enables the validation of a large number of adaptively chosen hypotheses, while provably avoiding overfitting.

claims.claim: LiveBench maintains contamination-free evaluation by using frequently updated questions from recent math competitions, arXiv papers, news articles, and datasets, with questions added and updated monthly.
claims.quote: LiveBench contains questions that are based on recently-released math competitions, arXiv papers, news articles, and datasets, and it contains harder, contamination-free versions of tasks from previous benchmarks. Questions will be added and updated on a monthly basis.

claims.claim: Overtraining with fresh data reduces the effects of test set contamination on generative evaluations, whereas supervised fine-tuning on the training set can increase or decrease performance depending on pretraining contamination amount.
claims.quote: Using scaling laws, we make a surprising discovery: including even a single test set replica enables models to achieve lower loss than the irreducible error of training on the uncontaminated corpus. We then study further training: overtraining with fresh data reduces the effects of contamination.

claims.claim: N-Day-Bench pulls fresh vulnerability cases monthly from GitHub security advisories, checks out repositories at the last commit before the patch, and uses a monthly refresh to keep the test set ahead of contamination.
claims.quote: Each month it pulls fresh cases from GitHub security advisories, checks out the repo at the last commit before the patch, and gives models a sandboxed bash shell to explore the codebase. The monthly refresh keeps the test set ahead of contamination — or at least makes the contamination window honest.

claims.claim: Decontamination efforts typically use n-gram matching to remove overlapping sentences and also translate test sets to delete translations from the training corpus, but semantic duplicates remain prevalent in training data.
claims.quote: By default this is just one level above string matching ("n-gram matching" - if sentences overlap in (say) a 13-token window, remove them from the training corpus). But you're actually trying, so you also translate the test sets and delete translations of test from train

claims.claim: AGI Gauntlet uses obfuscated, non-web prompt vectors to bypass dataset contamination and stress-test true executive reasoning past memorized training data.
claims.quote: Using obfuscated, non-web prompt vectors, it bypasses dataset contamination to stress-test true executive reasoning—pushing models past memorized training data to the precise point where their logic collapses.

claims.claim: TED (Trustworthy Evaluation via output Distribution) mitigates performance improvements from data contamination by correcting the LLM's output distribution, achieving up to 66.9% reduction in contamination-attributed gains.
claims.quote: To mitigate the impact of data contamination in evaluation, we also present TED: Trustworthy Evaluation via output Distribution, based on the correction of LLM's output distribution. TED substantially mitigates performance improvements up to 66.9% attributed to data contamination across various contamination setups.

claims.claim: Multiclass prediction problems are significantly more robust to overfitting from test set reuse than binary problems, with a new upper bound showing worst-case bias decreases with the number of classes.
claims.quote: We show a new upper bound of $\tilde O(\max\{\sqrt{k\log(n)/(mn)},k/n\})$ on the worst-case bias that any attack can achieve in a prediction problem with $m$ classes. Our experiments show that the additional uncertainty of prediction with a large number of classes indeed mitigates the effect of our best attacks.

claims.claim: New test sets built for CIFAR-10 and ImageNet by replicating the original data collection process reveal that all models experience an accuracy drop, indicating current benchmarks are susceptible to overfitting from dataset reuse.
claims.quote: We build new test sets for the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets and evaluate a broad range of classification models on the new datasets. All models experience a drop in accuracy, which indicates that current accuracy numbers are susceptible to even minute natural variations in the data distribution

claims.claim: String matching decontamination (n-gram overlap) is insufficient because simple variations like paraphrasing and translation of test data can bypass these measures and allow a 13B model to overfit benchmarks.
claims.quote: While most data decontamination efforts apply string matching (e.g., n-gram overlap) to remove benchmark data, we show that these methods are insufficient, and simple variations of test data (e.g., paraphrasing, translation) can easily bypass these decontamination measures.

claims.claim: A controlled method quantifies memorization and exploitation by pretraining BERT models on joint corpora of Wikipedia and labeled downstream datasets, then comparing performance on samples seen versus unseen during pretraining.
claims.quote: We pretrain BERT models on joint corpora of Wikipedia and labeled downstream datasets, and fine-tune them on the relevant task. Comparing performance between samples seen and unseen during pretraining enables us to define and quantify levels of memorization and exploitation.

open_questions: How do benchmark organizers coordinate fresh data collection at scale across diverse domains beyond coding and math?
What are the long-term dynamics of contamination as models train on synthetic data generated by other contaminated models?
How can held-out practices be standardized for agent benchmarks that involve multi-step interactions rather than static test sets?
What economic or governance models sustain continuous fresh benchmark creation given the cost of human annotation?
How do decontamination methods handle semantic equivalence that evades n-gram and translation-based filtering?
